questions.stem: Which capsule is polypeptide rather than polysaccharide?
questions.solutionHtml: n: Most capsules are polysaccharide; B. anthracis has poly-D-glutamate. (S. pyogenes capsule = hyaluronic acid polysaccharide, poorly immunogenic.)

questions.stem: Acid-fastness of mycobacteria is mainly due to:

options.label: C
options.text: Mycolic acids & complex lipids (e.g., cord factor) in the cell wall

questions.answerText: Mycolic acids & complex lipids (e.g., cord factor) in the cell wall
questions.solutionHtml: The lipid-rich wall with mycolic acids retains carbolfuchsin despite acid-alcohol decolorization (Ziehl–Neelsen/Kinyoun). Teichoic acids are Gram-positive features; hyaluronic acid capsule is seen in S. pyogenes.
Eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions (Negri). Post-exposure prophylaxis prevents disease if given promptly.

questions.stem: The most reliable method to sterilize heat-sensitive, moisture-sensitive plastic catheters is:
questions.solutionHtml: Gamma rays sterilizes without heat and penetrates plastics and complex lumens. Dry heat/autoclave damage heat-/moisture-sensitive materials; boiling is disinfection, not sterilization.

questions.stem: Pasteurization of milk by Holder method involves:
questions.solutionHtml: Holder method: 63°C for 30 minutes. HTST: 72°C for 15 sec.
Geobacillus stearothermophilus is the biological indicator for Autoclave.
Immune complex (Ag-Ab) deposition with complement activation → fever, rash, arthralgia: classic Type III.

questions.stem: Live attenuated vaccines are preferred when:

options.label: B
options.text: Cellular immunity is needed (e.g., intracellular pathogens)

questions.answerText: Cellular immunity is needed (e.g., intracellular pathogens)
questions.solutionHtml: : Live vaccines elicit robust CMI and mucosal responses; avoid in pregnancy/immunocompromise.

options.text: Patient antibody against a known antigen

questions.answerText: Patient antibody against a known antigen
questions.solutionHtml: Indirect ELISA coats plate with antigen, then detects patient antibodies via enzyme-linked anti-Ig.

questions.stem: Protein A of Staphylococcus aureus binds:
questions.solutionHtml: Protein A binds Fc region of IgG, hindering opsono-phagocytosis.
Diphtheria toxin inactivates EF-2 → halts protein synthesis → pseudomembrane, myocarditis, neuropathy.
Listeria grows at low temperatures; shows tumbling motility and actin rockets intracellularly.

questions.stem: Bacillus anthracis unique capsule is made of:
questions.solutionHtml: Anthrax capsule is a polypeptide (poly-D-glutamate), antiphagocytic and unusual among bacteria.

options.text: Double zone hemolysis on blood agar

questions.answerText: Double zone hemolysis on blood agar
questions.solutionHtml: C. perfringens produces α-toxin; shows characteristic inner complete and outer partial hemolysis.

options.text: Honey with spores → in vivo toxin production

questions.answerText: Honey with spores → in vivo toxin production
questions.solutionHtml: Infants ingest spores (often honey); germinate and produce toxin in the gut (floppy baby syndrome).
Chocolate agar with antibiotics (VCN) suppresses contaminants to isolate Neisseria species.

options.text: X and V factors; satellitism with S. aureus

questions.answerText: X and V factors; satellitism with S. aureus
questions.solutionHtml: Needs hemin (X) and NAD (V). S. aureus secretes V and releases X by hemolysis → satellitism.
Cholera toxin activates adenylate cyclase via Gs, causing secretory watery diarrhea (“rice water”).
C. jejuni infection is a common antecedent of GBS and can also cause reactive arthritis.

questions.stem: Helicobacter pylori best noninvasive test for active infection:
questions.solutionHtml: Urea breath or stool antigen detect active infection; IgG indicates exposure, not necessarily active disease.
Causes RLQ pain mimicking appendicitis; psychrotrophic, survives/transmits via refrigerated foods.
Brucella from unpasteurized dairy and animal tissues; undulant fever; intracellular pathogen.
Fastidious, needs cysteine; zoonotic (rabbits, ticks); ulceroglandular disease.

questions.stem: Legionella pneumophila features include all except:

options.label: A
options.text: Growth on BCYE with iron and cysteine

questions.solutionHtml: : No person-to-person spread; acquired from aerosols in water systems. Pontiac fever = self-limited febrile illness.
Cord factor correlates with virulence; mycolic acids and sulfatides inhibit phagolysosome fusion.

questions.stem: A DNA virus that replicates in the cytoplasm:
questions.solutionHtml: : Poxviruses carry their own transcription machinery → cytoplasmic replication.
HBV is a partially double-stranded DNA virus that uses reverse transcription in its life cycle.

questions.stem: HAV is distinguished from other enteroviruses by being:
questions.solutionHtml: HAV (a picornavirus) is acid-stable, spread fecal-orally; non-enveloped.

questions.stem: Antigenic shift in influenza results from:
questions.solutionHtml: Shift = reassortment (pandemics); drift = point mutations (seasonal outbreaks).
: SSPE occurs years after infection; vitamin A reduces acute morbidity in children.

questions.stem: Dengue severe disease risk increases with:

options.label: B
options.text: Secondary infection with a heterologous serotype

questions.answerText: Secondary infection with a heterologous serotype
questions.solutionHtml: : Antibody-dependent enhancement with heterologous secondary infection predisposes to severe dengue.

questions.stem: HBsAg positive, anti-HBc IgM positive suggests:
questions.solutionHtml: IgM anti-HBc indicates acute/recent infection. Vaccinees lack anti-HBc.
gp120 binds CD4 and co-receptors (CCR5 early, CXCR4 later). p24 antigen helps detect early infection.

questions.solutionHtml: Congenital CMV: growth restriction, SNHL, periventricular calcifications. Rubella = cataracts/PDA.
Zoster (shingles) results from waning CMI; dermatomal vesicular rash.

questions.stem: Key feature of Candida albicans is
questions.solutionHtml: Germ tube positivity at 37°C helps identify C. albicans/dubliniensis.

questions.stem: Morphology of Cryptococcus neoformans under microscopy is

options.label: A
options.text: Narrow-based budding yeast; India ink halo; latex antigen positive

questions.answerText: Narrow-based budding yeast; India ink halo; latex antigen positive
questions.solutionHtml: Encapsulated yeast from pigeon droppings; CSF antigen test is sensitive.
: Acute (≈45°) branching septate hyphae; ABPA, aspergilloma, invasive aspergillosis.

questions.stem: Major predisposing factor for Mucor/Rhizopus infection is
questions.solutionHtml: : Rhinocerebral mucormycosis thrives in high glucose/acidic milieu and with excess available iron.
